blocks.text: 14 November 2026 · North Seymour and Bachas or South Plaza and Carrion Point
A boat excursion is included. You’ll take one of two routes, both offering plenty to see. We confirm which route you’ll take after booking.

Visit North Seymour Island and the beaches of Las Bachas. We’ll take a bus to our yacht at the Itabaca Channel, then sail for about an hour to North Seymour.
We’ll land on a rocky shore near a small grove of grey and silver palo santo trees, which are leafless for most of the year.
North Seymour is known for its colonies of seabirds. Male frigatebirds use their red throat pouches to attract females during the mating season. The island is also home to blue-footed boobies, which have wedge-shaped tails and long, pointed wings. During courtship, a male raises one wing and one blue foot and dances to impress the female. The excursion continues to a beach with low cliffs, where you may see gulls, sea lions, marine iguanas and pelicans. Many of these animals can be seen at close range.
A freshly prepared lunch is served aboard the yacht.
After lunch, while you relax, the yacht continues to Las Bachas on the north coast of Santa Cruz Island. First, we’ll walk to a lagoon behind the beach that flamingos often visit. Then you can swim and snorkel from the uninhabited white-sand beach in turquoise water. You may see sea lions, several kinds of rays, sea turtles and tropical fish.
Return to Puerto Ayora at around 16:00. There’s time to stroll along the pier, shop for souvenirs or watch the sunset.
